The smallest such $n$ is 104. I am recalling this from the known competition problem (HMMT) and only sanity-checked the scale, so the result is not derived here.

Let $T_n$ denote the tower of $n$ twos. The comparison is between $T_n$ and the 100-fold iterated factorial of $100!$. Applying one more factorial roughly adds one more level to the tower, since $\log_2(m!) \approx m\log_2 m$. About 100 applications therefore raise the tower height by about 100 over the starting value.

As a sanity check on scale, $100! \approx 9.3\times10^{157}$, which is below $T_5 = 2^{65536} \approx 10^{19728}$. The starting value already sits at a tower height of about 4, so about 100 more factorials put the target near height 104.

ANSWER: 104
